violated_contract: A user-facing preference persisted optimistically before the operation that actually applies it completes must be rolled back to its prior value when that operation fails. `ChatProvider.switchBridgeMode` wrote the new `bridgeMode` (the `@AppStorage`-backed Settings preference) before calling `resolvedAgentClient().restart()`, and left it at the new value even when `restart()` threw `requestAlreadyActive` (a chat request in flight) — the internal truth trackers (`activeBridgeHarness`/`activeProviderMode`) were correctly left unchanged on that path, but the persisted preference the Settings picker and a future cold launch read was not, so it permanently disagreed with which provider was actually running.
canonical_prevention: Capture the prior persisted value before optimistically writing the new one, and restore it in the failure path of the apply operation before surfacing the error, so a failed apply leaves persisted state and actual runtime state in agreement. Reaching the failure path behaviorally requires a registered, live runtime with a genuinely in-flight request; where that seam does not exist, a labeled source-inspection test pinning the capture-before-write ordering and the rollback assignment inside the specific catch block is the documented fallback (see the two prior source-inspection tests for this same function's ordering/no-op-guard invariants).
